headline: Your growth plate
body: It doesn't just receive hormones from your bloodstream. It manufactures them on site.
punch: And vitamin D is one of the things controlling that.

headline: Most people picture hormones
body: Made in a gland, shipped through blood, received by tissue. Tissue as a passive endpoint waiting for instructions.

headline: Growth plate chondrocytes
body: Directly. Measured in isolated rat costochondral growth plate cells. The cartilage is an endocrine site, not just a target of one.
punch: The tissue that estrogen closes is also a tissue that makes estrogen.

headline: And the regulator
body: 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 regulates that local estradiol production — putting vitamin D upstream of local estrogen signalling in cartilage.
punch: A nutrient sitting upstream of a hormone nobody connects it to.

headline: This also explains
body: Blood hormone levels often correlate poorly with what a tissue is actually experiencing. Local production and local conversion can diverge from what a blood test shows.
punch: A serum number is not a growth plate measurement.

headline: Cartilage does this
body: Both articular and growth plate cartilage actively convert testosterone into DHT locally, with DHT the dominant metabolite that accumulates there.
punch: Local conversion is the rule in this tissue, not the exception.

headline: Which reframes
body: Asking what your circulating hormone levels are may be asking the wrong thing. What matters is what the tissue makes and converts where the growth happens.

headline: The limits
body: This is rat cell-culture work. It establishes the machinery exists and is vitamin-D-responsive. It does not quantify how much of human growth plate estrogen is locally made.
